correctness.rationale: For each admissible geometric PGF f_i(s)=1-m_i(1-s)/(1+a_i(1-s)), a_i>0,0<m_i<=1+a_i, composition is F_{M,C} with M=prod m_i and C=sum_i a_pi(i) prod_{j>i}m_pi(j). Adjacent exchange changes C by T a_i a_j (theta_j-theta_i), theta=(m-1)/a, T>0, so descending theta uniquely orders unequal-score seasons to minimize C globally, maximizing M/(1+C) terminal survival, minimizing convex order via stop-loss M(C/(1+C))^t, minimizing variance M(1+2C-M), and when repeated M>1 maximizing (M-1)/C perpetual survival. Opposite order extrema and equal-score ties follow. Independent exact Fraction composition/example (3,7),(2,2) yields best M=6,C=13 vs C=16, terminal 3/7 vs6/17, perpetual 5/13 vs5/16. The finite check is not a real-parameter exhaustive proof.

originality.rationale: Keiding–Nielsen 1973/1975 is a very close primary antecedent and explicitly proves fractional-linear composition and varying-environment extinction formulas. Its newly accessed complete 193-line article mathematical statements in Sections 1–4 do not assert a fixed-multiset permutation sorting theorem, sharp adjacent equality or convex-order extrema; an example compares two compositions locally, so the source is credited rather than declared unrelated. Prior general process theory is distinct from globally optimizing a deterministic season ordering.
